text:
sarah: Heads-up: docs PR #3012 (model rollout / canary guide) is blocked. Reviewers are asking for exact precedence rules for rollout windows vs. route-level overrides. Need runtime confirmation before I can ship the migration section.

omar: what's the ambiguous part? can you paste the paragraph?

sarah: current draft says:
"A canary rollout applies the route's rollout_window and traffic_percent. Route-level overrides take precedence over global defaults."

Review responses: they want: 1) if a project has a global default `rollout_window=7d` and a route sets `rollout_window=24h`, which wins, 2) if a canary is started via API with an explicit `end_time`, does that trump route `rollout_window`, and 3) how do overlapping canaries behave (two canaries for same route)?

phil: runtime short answers: 1) precedence: explicit route config wins over global defaults. 2) an API-provided explicit `end_time` overrides both route and global window for that rollout instance only. 3) overlapping canaries: the runtime enforces a single active canary per route. If you start a second canary while one is active, the API will either reject the second canary (default) or, if `force=true`, will replace the existing canary. We should document both behaviors and the `force` flag semantics.

sarah: helpful. can you confirm how metrics/rollbacks are handled if a forced replace happens mid-window? reviewers want to know whether the rollout history is preserved.

phil: replacing an active canary creates a new rollout record and marks the old rollout as `replaced` in the history with a timestamp and reason. Metrics for the replaced window remain attached to the original rollout record. The new rollout starts fresh with its own ID. We'll include an example history object in docs.

omar: also want to be explicit about traffic_percent semantics: when a canary is created with `traffic_percent=10`, is that percent of requests or percent of concurrent capacity?

phil: good call: it is percent of requests routed (based on sampling) not capacity. Under heavy load sampling is approximate but runtime targets the configured request percentage. If you need capacity guarantees use Dedicated reserved pools or explicit capacity routing.

docs-reviewer-zoe: this is great. please add a small YAML example showing (a) route-level override, (b) API snippet showing `end_time` override, and (c) the `force` replace example. We also want the exact error code / message the API returns when overlap is attempted without `force`.

sarah: adding examples now. Draft samples: YAML route override:
```yaml
global_defaults:
  rollout_window: 7d
routes:
  - name: payments-chat
    model: r-chat-1
    rollout_window: 24h
```
API canary creation with explicit end_time (curl):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/rollouts \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"route":"payments-chat","traffic_percent":10,"end_time":"2025-06-01T12:00:00Z"}'
```
Attempt to start overlapping canary without force returns 409 Conflict with body `{"error":"canary_in_progress","rollout_id":"r-123"}`. Use `force=true` to replace.

docs-reviewer-zoe: add a short callout: "Use force sparingly; replacing canaries may complicate metrics." Also ask runtime to confirm the 409 shape and field names.

phil: confirmed: 409 Conflict with JSON `{"error":"canary_in_progress", "active_rollout_id": "<id>"}`. We'll match that in the docs.

ci-bot: docs-preview: linter flagged missing timezone normalization note for `end_time`.

sarah: good catch. will add: "end_time must be an RFC3339 UTC timestamp; server will reject non-UTC values with 400."

phil: also adding that `end_time` is validated against route `rollout_window` max if set; if you pass an `end_time` beyond the max allowed window the API will return 422.

docs-reviewer-zoe: perfect. once you add the examples and the 409/422 shapes I'll re-review. If CI passes I'll approve and merge.

ci-bot: docs-preview: linkcheck passed, linter passed after timezone note.

docs-reviewer-zoe: approved. merging when you confirm no other changes.

sarah: merging now. thanks all for the quick responses.

phil: runtime note: no rollout behavior changes planned this release; changing canary semantics requires cross-team coordination.
